body: A real smile (Duchenne): the corners of the mouth lift, the cheeks rise, small crow's-feet appear at the outer eye corners and the eyes narrow slightly and shine; it builds over about half a second, holds with tiny changes and softens naturally – never a frozen grin. Shy smile: lips closed, eyes drop for a moment, then look back up.

Real laughter: the head tips back or forward, shoulders bounce with each breath of laughter, eyes squeeze almost shut, a hand may cover the mouth or touch a friend's arm; audible laughter in short bursts with breaths in between, then a smile and a recovering sigh. Children giggle higher and faster, older men laugh deep and slow.

Real crying or sadness: the chin trembles, the inner brows rise together, the lower lip pushes out, eyes become glossy and red-rimmed, a tear forms at the inner corner and runs down the cheek following the face's shape; breathing becomes uneven with small catches and sniffs, the person wipes the eye with a finger or the back of the hand and looks down.

Real surprise: eyebrows shoot up, eyes open wide showing white above the iris, the mouth drops open and a quick in-breath is audible, the head pulls back slightly; after a second the face resolves into joy (smile, hand to chest) or worry (frown) – surprise never lasts more than a moment.

Real anger or annoyance (kept non-violent): brows pulled down and together, eyes fixed, jaw tight, lips pressed, nostrils flaring, faster breathing, sharper hand gestures, a step forward; it cools with a long exhale, a head shake or a turn away.

Real fear: eyes wide and darting, brows raised and drawn together, lips stretched back, fast shallow breathing, shoulders up, the body leans or steps back, hands come up protectively or grab someone close.

Warm affection between two people (modest, respectful): soft eyes held a moment longer, a gentle smile, heads slightly tilted toward each other, relaxed shoulders, a light touch on the hand or arm, a shared laugh; they mirror each other's posture. Keep it tasteful and culturally modest.

Thinking or unsure: eyes go up and to the side, a finger taps the chin or lips, brows knit, the mouth twists to one side, a slow 'hmm' breath; then the eyes come back and the face lights up with the idea (eyebrows rise, a small nod, a pointing finger).

Tired: heavy slow blinks, drooping eyelids, a yawn (mouth wide, eyes squeezed, hand covering the mouth, audible stretch-breath), shoulders down, slower movements, rubbing the eyes or neck, sinking into a chair.

Talking to camera like a real person: eye contact with the lens most of the time with natural glances away while thinking, eyebrows emphasise key words, the head nods and tilts with the rhythm of speech, hands gesture at chest height (open palms, counting on fingers, pointing to a product), a breath before each sentence, a small smile at the end; the body is not rigid – slight sway and weight shifts.

A real conversation: the listener looks at the speaker's eyes and mouth, nods at the right moments, reacts with small expressions (smile, raised brows, a short 'mm' or 'ee'), sometimes looks down to think; turns are natural – one stops, a short pause, the other answers; nobody stares blankly into space.

A real child (about 5–12): proportionally larger head and eyes, soft round cheeks, quick restless movement, fidgeting hands, looking around curiously, sudden big smiles, a higher light voice, sometimes looking at an adult for approval; clothes slightly loose or playful. Children are always shown safe, happy and supervised in context.

A real baby or toddler: chubby limbs with creases at wrists and knees, wispy hair, wide curious eyes that track faces, gummy or few-tooth smile, uncoordinated grabbing, babbling and cooing sounds, the head supported by an adult when held; toddlers wobble when they walk with arms out for balance.

A real elderly person: deep wrinkles around eyes and mouth, age spots, thinner skin over veins on the hands, grey or white hair, slower deliberate movement, careful steps, sometimes a walking stick or prayer beads (masbaha) turning in the fingers, a warm tired smile, a deeper slower voice with pauses; posture slightly bent.

Young people (18–25): energetic and expressive, quick reactions, phones in hand, casual trendy clothes, confident or playful body language, fast laughter, looking at each other for reactions, a lively quicker voice.

A believable crowd: every person is an individual with different age, clothes, height and activity (walking at different speeds, talking in pairs, checking phones, carrying bags); nobody moves in sync, faces in the background are soft-focus but correct, the murmur of many voices and footsteps underneath.
Calm, composed personality: slow controlled movements, upright relaxed posture, steady eye contact, small precise gestures, a soft low voice with pauses, a gentle closed-mouth smile.
Energetic, cheerful personality: quick movements, bouncing on the toes, big open gestures, wide smile and bright eyes, laughter between words, a faster louder voice with rising intonation.

Hands done right: five fingers each with correct length and knuckles, nails, natural rest pose with fingers slightly curled; when holding something the fingers wrap around it with visible pressure and the object's weight pulls the wrist; hands move with purpose (pick up, turn, offer, point) and rest naturally between actions.

Real eyes: moist surface with catch-lights, visible iris texture and limbal ring, slightly different reflections in each eye, eyelids that move with the gaze (upper lid follows when looking down), small saccades, natural blink rate, and a gaze that clearly points at something in the scene.

Real hair: individual strands at the edges and flyaways in backlight, weight and bounce when the head moves, it moves with wind in one direction, settles after movement; beards have texture and density variation, trimmed edges, a few grey hairs for older men.

Real skin in close-up: pores, fine vellus hair, subtle redness on nose, cheeks and ears, slight shine on the T-zone, natural under-eye texture, freckles or marks where fitting, Middle-Eastern skin tones rendered warm and varied (olive to deep brown) – never airbrushed plastic.

Women in hijab shown naturally and respectfully: the scarf wraps around the face with real fabric folds and a pin, it moves slightly with the head and wind, colours and patterns are specific (for example dusty rose chiffon, black crepe), make-up subtle or elegant, abaya fabric flows and swings with walking.

Wedding joy (Iraqi style): guests clapping in rhythm, women ululating (hilhola), men dancing in a line, children running between tables, the bride in a white gown and the groom in a suit greeting people, phones filming, confetti and lights; faces show real joy – laughter, tears of happiness, hugs.

Prayer shown with respect: calm still posture on a prayer rug, slow deliberate movements between standing, bowing and prostration, hands raised for dua with palms up, eyes lowered, quiet surroundings, soft light; no staging or mockery.

Iraqi greeting: a warm 'هلا والله' with a hand on the chest, men shake hands and may kiss cheeks (two or three times), a slight bow of the head to elders, women greet women with cheek kisses, children kiss the hand of grandparents; smiles and eye contact throughout.

Iraqi hospitality: the host stands to welcome guests, insists they sit in the best place, pours tea into small istikan glasses on saucers, offers dates, kleicha and fruit with both hands, says 'تفضلوا'; guests protest politely, then accept with a hand on the heart.

Real applause: hands clap at slightly different rhythms, people smile and nod, some whistle or cheer 'يا سلام', the sound swells and fades unevenly; the person being applauded looks moved, nods thanks with a hand on the chest.
